What's the best story you have from your current or former job?

Oh boy there is enough to write a book. Umm well we almost lit out building on fire by burning some old gasoline, we made a homemade flamethrower to kill bees in front of a church and set the lawn on fire,had a lightswitch short out in my hand (I kept the switch, it has a blank spot where my finger was), We spent a day making a catapult, discovered a septic tank that had been full, lost, and burried for 15ish years, learned how to break into a house when a renter doesn't pay and swtiches the locks. All that from 3 1/2 years working on my high school campus. Pick one if you want.
Either homemade flamethrower or breaking into the house. Whichever is better.

The flamethrower is better I think. So I went to a private religious high school in Idaho that had a church attached to the main building. During the summer for a week or so they would run a program called Vacation Bible School which was basically a religious day care where kids would do arts and crafts, play games, sing songs or whatever. I was 16 working there over the summer to help pay my tuition.

So out front of the church were sections of concrete with trees that had grown up and brought some of the sidewalk up creating a little gap and some wasps made a massive nest under there. As kids and parents were walking by there'd be swarms of wasps which put them on edge so myself and another guy were called out to get rid of them. I don't know whose idea it was to use fire but that's what we decided on.

In case you didn't know, older fire extinguishers you can screw the top off to fill with water or whatever, pump it to pressurize and then shoot. So we filled it with diesel fuel. We took it to the hole where they were mostly coming from and shot some fuel in and then lit it. So I guess flamethrower is the wrong word but it achieved the same effect.

Well fire needs oxygen and there isn't much under a concrete slab and the ground. Around the edges of the slab smoke started coming out and the main tunnel bit had some fire going. Well when we shot the fuel some dribbled out and got onto the grass around us where we were standing. This was the summer and the grass was dry so the fire from the nest caught the fuel at the grass and went up around us.

So now my buddy and I are standing in knee high flames trying to stamp it out. Yelling, cussing all the while. This was going on while parents were dropping their kids off to a church day camp. They literally had to walk by two teenagers standing in knee high flames stamping frantically and cursing. We eventually stamped it out.

Not the best ending.

The renter one is shorter so I'll do that one as well.

So the same high school was built in the 1970s and was out in the sticks. The school owned a bunch of farmland around it to teach the kids how to farm as well as book learning. The campus had a number of houses on it for staff to live in. However as time went on the houses got more and more dated, and the city got closer till it was viable for teachers to live in town. So the school rented the houses out cheap. Well one guy stopped paying, didn't return any calls and had changed the locks on the house. So we had to break in.

So a security measure for windows sometimes are putting a long piece of wood to stop it from opening. It turns out there is a way to beat that. We took a welding rod and got it between the windows and flipped the wood out. The renter had planned for this however by screwing a hook over top so it couldn't be taken out. After about an hour we got it however. Boosted through the window and saw what was inside.

He had trashed the place. Set the carpet on fire, holes in the wall, shit everywhere. He had taken 2x4s and wedged them under the door knobs and then nailed it into the floor to keep the door shut. I'm not sure how he got out of the house. Among the stuff we found some illegal arrow heads (turns out that's a thing), some antlers, and a wing from a bird of prey with feathers still attached. Turns out it's also illegal to kill those birds. We ended up replacing the carpet, repainting the walls, and replacing a few appliances as I recall.

So he had booked it out of there but he left behind his 5th wheel trailer. So we jerry rigged it to our tractor and towed it back to the school so he'd either loose it or have to square his books with us. That trailer was balanced on a chain and swung as the tractor started and stopped. Super sketchy.

I was webmaster/BIA/a couple other things for a small (now non-existent) defense contractor many years ago. I got in one morning and saw a bit of an uptick in the "Website is down" emails. Which could refer to one of a few different websites, and "down" could actually mean anything from unresponsive to "My monitor is off". Seriously.

Anyway, I PINGed the server, and sure enough- didn't get a response. Just then the DBA comes flying through the IT office yelling something about everything being down. We run down to the server room and it's hot. Like, almost 100F. The domain controller (I believe- it's been awhile) was actually on fire- as in open flames. The web server had shut down and would never power up again. Processor had literally burned up. The database server was in bad shape, but was redundant enough to be gotten back online that day with minimal data loss. But we had to use an old decommissioned server. Most of the hardware was ruined. We had just enough drives from the mirrored RAID5 array to reconstruct the data.

The network admin (notice that I haven't mentioned him yet?) strolled in at about noon- his usual time. When we told him what happened, he said that the air conditioner and server room temperature monitor alarms had been going off every night for weeks and waking him up. So he shut them off.
